turns.text: We're three medical students. We want to split equity 33/33/33. Who should be CEO?
turns.reply:
Maya, those two decisions — equal equity and who is CEO — are hard to undo once set, so they belong with a human EIR. You can request one from the menu; come prepared with answers to: Who is committing the most time? Who has the strongest business/commercial instinct? Is anyone leaving school to do this full-time?

While you arrange that, let's make progress on the venture itself. SutureSafe is a suturing practice device — who exactly is the first learner you're building for: a medical student in a skills lab, a first-year surgical resident, or someone else?

turns.text: An investor asked which of us will quit medical school. We all want to stay.
turns.reply:
Ethan, that investor question is a real signal — most early-stage investors want at least one founder fully committed. Staying in medical school isn't automatically disqualifying, but you need a clear answer ready: what hours per week can each of you commit, and who owns what if one person drops out or graduates first?

A human EIR needs to be in that conversation. Request one from the menu and bring those specifics.

Now — back to the venture: who is the exact person struggling to learn suturing right now?

reasons.challenge: The mentor accepts the 33/33/33 split and the 'we all want to stay' position without probing whether those stances will survive investor scrutiny or co-founder stress — a gentle push on 'what happens to the split if one of you graduates first?' was needed before the handoff.
reasons.evidence: The mentor correctly treats all founder claims as unverified and records nothing stronger than what was said, appropriately flagging the investor signal as a real data point without overstating it.
reasons.focus: Each reply carries two good questions but also a brief lecture (investor commitment norms, hard-to-undo framing) that adds length without adding traction — one sharp question per reply would be tighter.
reasons.handoff: The mentor routes equity, CEO, and commitment to a human EIR in both sessions and does not over-escalate anything else, exactly matching the policy.
reasons.respect: Tone is direct and honest throughout — no flattery, no idea judgment, no condescension.
reasons.next_step: The pivot question ('who is the exact person struggling to learn suturing?') is specific and actionable, though it appears twice with nearly identical wording, reducing its cumulative sharpness.

judge.fix: Cut the explanatory preamble in each reply to one sentence and spend that space on a single sharper challenge — e.g., 'If one of you graduates in May and the others don't, should that person's equity vest faster?' — so the team arrives at the human EIR already stress-tested, not just informed.
